description: Acknowledge a claimed thread and start its working clock (work_started_at): the current holder signals it has begun work, distinct from just holding the claim. Acknowledge as soon as you start: a leased claim left unacknowledged past the server's window (MAIDAN_CLAIM_ACK_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120 s) is reported to its owner with a claim_unacknowledged event. Only the assignee holding the matching fencing token may acknowledge; idempotent (the first start time is kept).

claim_lease_id.description: the fencing token from the claim response's thread.claim_lease_id

name: acknowledge_claim

description: Change a plan you already submitted, holding the plan thread's live claim (pass its lease_id). cancel names children to cancel; add gives new children (the shape submit_plan takes, depends_on may name any child of the plan); rewire sets a child's depends_on afresh. Cancel and add the same key to replace a child: its dependents wait for the new one. A cancelled child's dependents stop waiting for it. Only children that are open and unclaimed can be cancelled or rewired: a claimed or finished one is refused, as is a fourth amendment of the same plan (error code -32010). reason is kept on each cancelled child. Everything happens in one transaction, or nothing does. Added children are held for review when the plan is held or one of them needs a threat model.

depends_on.description: keys of any children in the plan

cancel.description: keys of unclaimed children to cancel

lease_id.description: the fencing token from your claim on the plan thread

reason.description: why the plan changed; kept on each cancelled child

thread_id.description: the plan thread you hold the claim on

name: amend_plan

description: Atomically claim the oldest claimable thread in a channel for a member (claimable = unassigned or its lease expired). Every claim is leased. Returns the claimed thread with a content-addressed pin {uri, content_hash}, or null when there is no claimable work. This tool takes work; it does not create it. Create a channel with create_channel and a task with create_thread (both need workspace:write; the REST twins are POST /workspaces/{wid}/channels and POST /channels/{cid}/threads).

engine.description: only claim a thread routed to this engine, for a worker that serves one kind of work; a thread routed to another engine, or not routed at all, is then never claimed. Omitted, any work

lane.description: the service lane this worker runs in; lane breaks ties, never filters: among threads of equal priority and wait, threads in this lane come first, then unlaned ones, then other lanes. Omitted, unlaned threads win the tie

lease_secs.description: lease in seconds (1 s to 7 days); renew before it lapses, or the thread is reaped and returns to the queue with a ClaimExpired. Omitted, the server's default lease applies (MAIDAN_CLAIM_DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS, 600 s)

repo.description: only claim a thread whose footprint names this repository (owner/name or a GitHub clone URL), for a worker whose checkout is that repository; a thread without a footprint is then never claimed. Omitted, any work

name: claim_next_thread

description: Atomically claim the oldest claimable thread across every channel of the workspace you may read (claim_next_thread for the whole workspace), so an agent serving the whole workspace makes one call instead of one per channel. The same filters (open, dependencies finished, skills held, no pending approval gate, not blocked or parked unclaimable, you not frozen), order, lease and fencing token. A private channel's threads go only to its members and a DM's only to its participants. Returns the claimed thread with a content-addressed pin {uri, content_hash}, or null when there is no claimable work.

engine.description: only claim a thread routed to this engine, for a worker that serves one kind of work; a thread routed to another engine, or not routed at all, is then never claimed. Omitted, any work

lane.description: the service lane this worker runs in; lane breaks ties, never filters: among threads of equal priority and wait, threads in this lane come first, then unlaned ones, then other lanes. Omitted, unlaned threads win the tie

lease_secs.description: lease in seconds (1 s to 7 days); renew before it lapses, or the thread is reaped and returns to the queue with a ClaimExpired. Omitted, the server's default lease applies (MAIDAN_CLAIM_DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS, 600 s)

repo.description: only claim a thread whose footprint names this repository (owner/name or a GitHub clone URL), for a worker whose checkout is that repository; a thread without a footprint is then never claimed. Omitted, any work

wait_ms.description: with nothing claimable, wait up to this long for work to become claimable (a new thread, a dependency finishing, a claim released or expiring) and claim it, instead of answering null at once. The claimant's wake-up: no polling loop. Omitted or 0, one try

name: claim_next_workspace_thread

description: Declare the agent's self-reported status on a thread: working, needs_input, needs_review, blocked, or done, with a one-sentence note. By the claim holder or owner; stalled is refused (system-computed only). Supersedes any prior declaration. Appends StatusDeclared. Requires thread:transition.

note.description: One-sentence description of what the agent is doing

name: declare_status

description: Poll a durable approval gate by id. Returns the gate — state is pending until a human answers, then accepted/declined/cancelled with any content they supplied — or null if no such gate exists in your workspace. Hosts with MCP Apps show it as an inline approval card.

gate_id.description: the gate id returned by request_approval

name: get_approval_gate

description: Pack thread messages, edits, references, FSM history, and the workspace glossary for agent prompts. Edits are lean by default (id/editor/timestamp only); pass include_edits=true for full before/after bodies. The glossary (canonical term definitions) is included by default when non-empty; pass include_glossary=false to drop it. Pass as_of=<event_id> to replay the thread as it stood at that event-log id (deterministic over the immutable log; audit / re-ask from before a tangent). Pass token_budget=<n> to cap the message page by estimated tokens: the opening message and the recent tail are kept, the middle is folded into an auditable elision marker in fixed blocks. The result is two text parts: the stable prefix (workspace boot, brief, messages) and the volatile tail (state, lease, cursors, prefix sha256). Those strings are the bytes REST returns with split=true.

as_of.description: Event-log id: reconstruct the thread as it stood at that point (as-of replay). Omit for the live pack.

delta.description: Return a delta instead of the whole pack. The first content part is always the delta head (delta, prefix_unchanged, prefix_sha256, prefix_bytes), never empty; the second is the volatile tail. When since_prefix_sha matches the current prefix, the head has prefix_unchanged true and no messages or prefix. With message_cursor, the head adds the messages after that cursor when appending them rebuilds the prefix; otherwise it carries the replacement prefix.

include_accepted_decisions.description: Attach in-channel accepted/closed decisions (token-lean teasers) so a fresh claimer sees what the channel already decided. Waiter envelopes appear only when status is reviewed; result_kind is a namespaced string (e.g. example.review.result/1), not a closed enum. Withheld on DM channels. Set false for the leanest pack.

include_edits.description: Include full body_before/body_after on each edit (heavy); default returns edit metadata only.

include_glossary.description: Include the workspace glossary (grounding); omitted when empty. Set false for a token-tight pack.

include_parent_grounding.description: For a child thread, attach parent grounding (the parent's opening ask + latest decision) so a fresh claimer knows why the thread exists. Absent for root threads / cross-channel / DM parents. Set false for the leanest pack.

max_bytes.description: Cap the canonical pack by bytes. Elision grows by fixed message blocks until the pack fits or only the opener and newest message remain.

message_cursor.description: Page messages after this id. With delta, it is also the delta cursor.

since_prefix_sha.description: Hex sha256 of a prefix the caller already holds. Requests a delta on its own.

token_budget.description: Cap the message page by estimated tokens (chars/4): keep the opening message and the recent tail, fold the middle into an auditable 'elision' marker. Omit to cap by rows only.

name: get_thread_context

description: The thread's active agent status declaration, or null when cleared. Requires workspace:read.
name: get_thread_status

description: Link an artifact your workspace holds to a thread as evidence, by its sha256. Upload it first; a hash your workspace does not hold is not found. Linking twice keeps the first link. Moves the thread's version. Requires workspace:write.
name: link_thread_artifact

description: List the workspace's live claims with their footprints (thread_id, assignee_id, lease_expires_at, repo, mode, items, attributes), in one repository when repo is given. Only threads you may read are listed. Use it to defer work whose footprint would overlap before claiming.

repo.description: owner/name, or a GitHub clone URL

name: list_active_claims

description: Post a message to a thread as the authenticated member.

body.description: plain text; omit when sending typed content (body is derived from it)

name: post_message

description: Release a claim (graceful handoff): the current holder returns the thread to the queue immediately by presenting its fencing token, instead of letting the lease lapse — e.g. an agent shutting down cleanly. Only the assignee holding the matching token may release. Clears the assignment and working clock and emits thread_assignment_changed.

claim_lease_id.description: the fencing token from the claim response's thread.claim_lease_id

name: release_claim

description: Extend a claimed thread's lease (heartbeat). Only the current assignee holding the matching fencing token may renew; a stale holder whose claim was reclaimed is rejected.

claim_lease_id.description: the fencing token from the claim response's thread.claim_lease_id

lease_secs.description: new lease deadline in seconds from now (1 s to 7 days)

name: renew_claim

description: Record one retry-safe usage heartbeat for your active claim. input is uncached input. Cache writes are a 5-minute tier and a 1-hour tier. Reuse usage_report_id only for an exact retry; claim_lease_id fences stale workers. Maidan derives reporter from auth and payer from the thread. The price snapshot must calculate to usd_micros. A token budget counts fresh tokens only. A binding cap atomically stops the run.

standard_price.description: the standard-tier price of a call in a cheaper lane (batch, or a batch or flex service_tier), so the usage rollup shows the lane saving as reported; refused on any other call, or if its charge for the reported tokens overflows or is below the charged amount

cache_read.description: cached input; not part of a token budget

name: report_usage

description: Human-in-the-loop gate: open a durable approval gate and return {status: input_required, gate_id} without blocking. A human resolves it later (accept/decline/cancel) over the /ui; poll get_approval_gate for the outcome. Silence is never consent. Pass thread_id to make it a claim gate — while the gate is pending, claim_next will not hand that thread to an agent.

prompt.description: what the human is being asked to approve

risk.description: how much a wrong accept would cost; omitted means high. The workspace's approval policy decides from it whether a model's accept through approval_decide needs a person to confirm it in the console

schema.description: optional JSON Schema for structured detail the human may supply alongside their decision

thread_id.description: optional thread to gate: while pending, claim_next skips this thread (a required-human claim gate)

name: request_approval

description: Replace a thread's task attributes in full. The kind says what sort of work it is (change, plan or review), the engine says who or what it is routed to (pi, session or human), and threat_model marks work that needs a threat model. A claim_next that names an engine takes only work routed to that engine, so a Pi worker is never handed session or human work. A thread nobody described reads as a change with no engine and no threat model.

acceptance.description: how a reviewer verifies the task; the worker must satisfy it

engine.description: omit to leave the work unrouted

lane.description: the service lane it may run in: batch (async, cheapest) or flex; omitted runs at standard rates

linear_issue.description: the Linear issue the task is for, such as ENG-123; where the workspace turned claim comments on, the claim and release are said on it

tier.description: the change's review tier; omitted reads as B in the metrics

name: set_thread_attributes

description: Declare what part of a repository this thread's work touches, so a swarm claiming from one queue never holds overlapping work. items lists {kind: path|glob|crate|lane|branch, value}; lane, crate and branch match exactly, path and glob by prefix (a glob counts up to its first wildcard). mode exclusive conflicts with any overlap, shared only with an exclusive one, and a branch is always exclusive. Footprints count only while the thread holds a live claim and free themselves when it ends. claim_next skips a thread whose footprint overlaps a live claim. On a claimed thread, a footprint that overlaps another live claim is refused with error code -32009 and data.conflicts (each with thread_id, assignee_id, lease_expires_at, kind, value), and nothing is stored: release the claim and requeue, or narrow the footprint. No items clears the footprint. repo is owner/name, or a GitHub clone URL.

kind.description: slot names a shared resource such as a build slot (rust-build), counted across the workspace against the capacity an operator set; the others name part of the repository

repo.description: owner/name, or a GitHub clone URL

name: set_thread_footprint

description: Attach a task's structured result (arbitrary JSON). Upserts one result per thread and notifies waiters via a thread_result_set event. Use when finishing a task so a requester or parent can read the output. Fenced by your claim: pass claim_lease_id from the claim response; if the lease lapsed and someone else took the thread (or it was released), the call is refused (claim_lost) and nothing is stored, so stop the work.

claim_lease_id.description: the fencing token from the claim response's thread.claim_lease_id

name: set_thread_result

description: Make every child of a plan thread in one call. Only the member holding the plan thread's live claim can plan it, passing that claim's lease_id. Each child has a key unique in the plan, a title, and optional description, attributes, footprint and depends_on (keys of other children in the same plan). Children are created in the plan thread's channel with their dependency edges, so dependents stay off the queue until what they depend on lands; a child that closes without landing blocks its dependents, and the plan thread closes itself when its last child lands. Every child repository must be on this workspace's github_branch egress allowlist. A bad child, an unknown or cyclic depends_on, or too many children for the spawn budget creates nothing. Calling again from the same claim with the same keys answers the children already made (replayed: true); any other plan on a thread that has children is refused with error code -32010 and data.children.

attributes.description: the child's task attributes (the shape set_thread_attributes takes, without thread_id)

depends_on.description: keys of children that must land first

footprint.description: the child's footprint (the shape set_thread_footprint takes, without thread_id)

key.description: unique within this plan; depends_on names children by key

test.description: the command that proves the child done; kept in its description

lease_id.description: the fencing token from your claim on the plan thread

thread_id.description: the plan thread (kind plan) you hold the claim on

name: submit_plan

description: Advance a thread's FSM state (start_review, close, or archive). The MCP twin of REST POST /threads/:id. Separation of duties, the required-reviewers close-gate, and unresolved refutes all apply identically — there is no MCP bypass. On a thread with a review requirement, start_review is refused until a result is posted (set_thread_result). Returns the updated thread.

action.description: start_review (open to in_review), close (in_review to closed) or archive (closed to archived). To send work back, use submit_review with request_changes

name: transition_thread

description: Block until a task becomes ready (its last blocking dependency reaches a terminal state, emitting thread_ready), or the timeout lapses. Returns the ThreadReady event, or null on timeout. Scoped to channel_id when given, else any accessible thread in the workspace. Pass since_log_id (your high-water log_id) to also catch readiness signalled in the gap before this call subscribes; omit it for pure-live (pick up already-ready work with claim_next_thread first). To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait.

channel_id.description: optional: scope to one channel's tasks

since_log_id.description: lookback anchor: replay the log for a matching event with log_id greater than this before parking live

name: wait_for_ready

description: Return the authentication-bound identity: actor_id, member_id, optional delegation_grant_id, workspace_id, capabilities, capability_sets the caller fully holds, and whether the credential is a bearer. Call this first — writes are attributed to member_id.
name: whoami
